change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The driver torque response time limit was reduced from 100 ms to 80 ms for accelerator pedal demand above 70%. Verification tests for torque response latency must update their pass thresholds and re-evaluate baseline evidence against the new 80 ms limit.

assessments.reason: The test directly verifies VCU-DR-01 and uses a 100 ms script threshold, but VCU-DR-01 was tightened to 80 ms. The previous PASS result of 94 ms exceeds the new 80 ms requirement limit and is no longer valid.
evidence: Requirement VCU-DR-01 tightened threshold from 100 ms to 80 ms
TV-001 procedure specifies 100 ms limit and comment notes '100 ms threshold in script'
Previous result recorded PASS (94 ms), which fails the new 80 ms requirement
assessments.recommended_action: Update the test procedure and automated script threshold to 80 ms, then re-run the test.

assessments.reason: The test links to VCU-DR-01 and applies 85% pedal demand (exceeding the 70% threshold), but timing was not recorded in previous baseline evidence. It is uncertain whether the response latency complies with the tightened 80 ms requirement.
evidence: TV-002 links to VCU-DR-01 and applies 85% pedal demand
Comment notes 'Timing not reported in old evidence'
assessments.recommended_action: Re-run the arbitration test with high-resolution latency logging to measure exact torque command response time against the 80 ms limit.

assessments.reason: The test procedure sweeps pedal demand 75-95% and measures torque response latency, directly exercising VCU-DR-01 despite a missing link from migration. Its existing threshold of 95 ms and previous evidence of 92 ms are invalidated by the tightened 80 ms limit.
evidence: Procedure sweeps demand 75-95% (above VCU-DR-01 70% threshold)
Previous result recorded PASS (92 ms) with legacy 95 ms tolerance
Workshop note confirms high-load campaign lost requirement hyperlinks during migration
assessments.recommended_action: Restore requirement link to VCU-DR-01, update test threshold to 80 ms, and re-execute high-load test suite.

assessments.reason: This test measures emergency brake command latency under VCU-BRK-03, which is unchanged. Workshop notes explicitly clarify that brake latency uses a different measurement clock and must not be conflated with driver torque response time.
evidence: Linked requirement VCU-BRK-03 is unchanged
Comment states 'Different measurement clock'
Workshop note states brake command latency and positive torque command latency use different clocks and must not be conflated
assessments.recommended_action: No action required; retain existing test procedure and baseline result.

assessments.reason: The test verifies degraded mode entry and fault logging upon wheel-speed sensor failure under requirement VCU-DGN-04, which remains unchanged.
evidence: Linked requirement VCU-DGN-04 is unchanged
Procedure checks degraded mode and fault log upon sensor disconnect

assessments.reason: The test verifies mode change logging and software build recording under requirement VCU-LOG-05, which is unchanged.
evidence: Linked requirement VCU-LOG-05 is unchanged
Procedure verifies logging of timestamp and build identifier during Comfort to Sport transition

assessments.reason: Requirement link is marked TBD and test ownership is unclarified. Although the procedure uses 80% pedal demand (above the 70% threshold of VCU-DR-01), traceability and applicable requirements must be established by an authorized owner.
evidence: Requirement reference is TBD
Comment states 'Ownership and source link to be clarified'
Procedure applies 80% pedal demand under elevated thermal load
assessments.recommended_action: Review with system engineer to assign formal requirement linkage and test ownership before evaluating 80 ms latency applicability under thermal load.

assessments.reason: Traceability is broken because the test links to VCU-OLD-88, an unknown requirement from a legacy catalog. Relevance to current requirements cannot be determined without human review.
evidence: Requirement reference VCU-OLD-88 is marked unknown_requirement
Comment notes 'Imported row; requirements catalog changed'
assessments.recommended_action: Re-map test to active requirements catalog or archive the test if obsolete.

assessments.reason: The test verifies qualitative torque ramp profile differences between Sport and Comfort modes under VCU-MOD-06 (unchanged) and contains no quantitative response-time assertion.
evidence: Linked requirement VCU-MOD-06 is unchanged
Comment confirms 'No quantitative response-time assertion'

assessments.reason: The test evaluates input filtering of false pedal spikes shorter than 10 ms under unchanged requirement VCU-DR-02.
evidence: Linked requirement VCU-DR-02 is unchanged
Procedure tests 7 ms transient pulse filtering
Comment confirms 'Pedal sampling test only'

assessments.reason: The test evaluates positive torque suppression when emergency braking is requested, verifying brake override priority under unchanged requirement VCU-BRK-03.
evidence: Linked requirement VCU-BRK-03 is unchanged
Procedure verifies positive torque drop according to brake priority

assessments.reason: The test measures ECU power-cycle boot readiness within 500 ms, which evaluates platform startup and is completely unrelated to driver torque response time VCU-DR-01.
evidence: Procedure verifies readiness within 500 ms after ECU power cycle
Comment notes 'Platform startup only'
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for VCU-DR-01 change; assign appropriate platform requirement link during register cleanup.
